findings.message: The learner asked for stochastic gradient descent, but the noise is scaled to the slope (1 + sd·gauss), so it disappears near the minimum. Real minibatch noise does not disappear there: at a fixed rate, SGD keeps wandering around the minimum, and that is the main sign of SGD. At the default batch of 16 the noise is only 7.5%, so the Next step and Full-batch step arrows overlap here and look the sa
Not sampled: changing the batch size, the lowest learning rate (0.01) and the New run / kept-path comparison. These captures never show the batch size control having an effect.

At batch 16 the run path is an almost straight line to the minimum, the same as full-batch descent, so the 'stochastic' part of the request cannot be seen. This comes from the noise being proportional to the slope (see v0-s0).

The assumption says an off-bowl path point is 'drawn at the rim, where the ball is held'. In fact lift() sets its height to TOP (3.74), while the ball is held on the surface at y=2.32 (x=2, z=0.47). The last trail point floats above the rim, away from the ball, so the picture contradicts the stated assumption. The trail point should use the surface height at the clamped (x, z): K·loss(rim x, rim z

The top-right trail segment ends in the air beyond the bowl edge (about pixel 670,222), clearly apart from the red ball (about 640,285). The path does not lead to the ball, which makes the divergence hard to read.
Same problem as v0-s0: the noise disappears with the slope, and at the default batch the two step arrows cannot be told apart, so SGD's stochastic behaviour is not shown.
The path is smooth and noiseless at batch 16, which is not what SGD looks like (see v0-s0).
Off-bowl trail points are lifted to TOP instead of the rim surface height where the ball is held, so the last path point floats above the bowl and does not match the assumption.
The final trail point is in the air above the rim, separate from the ball held on the surface.
